newsitem.title: INDIA: India gives incentive for early sugarcane crushing.
newsitem.headline: India gives incentive for early sugarcane crushing.

text.p: The Indian government has decided to provide incentives to sugar factories for early crushing of sugarcane between October 1 and November 15, 1997, the Food Ministry said on Wednesday.

"The incentive will be in the form of a higher free sale quota at the rate of 72 percent as against the normal 60 percent on the entire sugar production during the period," the ministry said in a statement.
The statement said this had been done to maximise sugar production in the 1997/98 (October-September) season and safeguard the interests of sugarcane growers.

Industry officials expect India's sugar output in the 1996/97 season to dip sharply to about 12.8 million tonnes from the previous year's record 16.45 million. But there is no fear of shortage since India held plenty of carryover stocks.
